1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The EJR condition (for n=10, k=5) requires that any cohesive group S of size at least ℓ·2 whose members share at least ℓ commonly approved candidates must have at least one member of S who is represented by ≥ℓ candidates in W. The largest such group is the 6-voter set {1,2,3,8,9,10} sharing exactly the three x-candidates. This forces |W ∩ {x1,x2,x3}| ≥ 2 (otherwise no voter in the group can reach representation 3). Consequently voter 1, whose approvals intersect this set in exactly those three candidates, is guaranteed at least one seat from the x-candidates, establishing a lower bound of 1.  

An explicit EJR committee attaining the lower bound is W = {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1}: every ℓ-cohesive group of the requisite size is represented at the demanded level, yet voter 1 approves only two members. Upper-bound examples such as W = {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} likewise satisfy EJR while giving voter 1 four approved members. No EJR committee can give voter 1 all five (the remaining cohesive groups of size 4 force at least one y-candidate outside A1). Hence the feasible range for voter 1 is 1–4.

B. min 1, max 4

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The EJR condition for the group of 6 voters {1,2,3,8,9,10} (who all approve the same 3 x-candidates) requires that at least one voter in the group approves ≥3 members of W. This is impossible unless W contains at least 2 of the x-candidates; the only ways to reach a representation of 3 for some member of the group without voter 1 receiving 3 are combinations such as 2 x-candidates + z1. Thus voter 1's representation is at least 2.

The group of 4 voters {4,5,6,7} (who share 3 y-candidates) likewise requires that some member of the group approves ≥2 members of W, so W must contain at least 2 candidates from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}. This constraint can be met while still placing 3 x-candidates + y1 inside W, giving voter 1 a total of 4 approved members. No larger number is feasible.

Hence the possible range is exactly min 2, max 4 (choice A).

(The other large cohesive groups impose no tighter bounds on voter 1.)

1.text:
The EJR analysis for the ℓ=3 cohesive group of size 6 ({voters 1-3,8-10}, all sharing exactly the three x-candidates) requires that at least one member of the group receives ≥3 representatives in W. With only a single x-candidate in W, even voters 8-10 (who alone can supplement with z1) reach at most representation 2, violating EJR. Hence at least two x-candidates must enter W; because voters 1-3 approve none of the supplementary z/y fillers usable by 8-10, voter 1 is guaranteed those two x-candidates (lower bound = 2).

The symmetric ℓ=2 cohesive group of size 4 ({voters 4-7}) forces at least two members of W from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}, but this quota can be met while still placing three x-candidates plus y1 (or z3) inside W, giving voter 1 representation 4. No EJR committee attains representation 5 for voter 1 (the y-group quota cannot be satisfied without a non-approved candidate). Thus the feasible range under EJR is exactly 2-4.

A. min 2, max 4

2.text:
The ℓ=3 cohesive group of size 6 ({1,2,3,8,9,10}, sharing exactly {x1,x2,x3}) requires that at least one voter in the group is represented ≥3 times by any EJR committee W.  

- If |W ∩ {x1,x2,x3}| = 1, the only way to meet the threshold is to also include both y1 and z3 (so that voter 1 reaches representation exactly 3). All other voters in the group reach at most 2. Thus any such W necessarily gives voter 1 exactly 3 approved members.  
- If |W ∩ {x1,x2,x3}| ≥ 2, the threshold can be met without using y1 or z3 (e.g., voters 8–10 reach representation 3 once z1 is also taken). This permits W to give voter 1 as few as 2 approved members, as witnessed by the explicit EJR committee {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1}.  

Hence no EJR committee can give voter 1 only 1 approved member, establishing a lower bound of 2.  

The matching upper bound of 4 is realized by committees such as {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} (which satisfies the ℓ=3 group because voter 1 reaches representation 5) while the remaining size-4 cohesive groups force at least one non-approved member into W, so 5 is impossible.  

Thus the feasible range is exactly 2–4.
